description: Query large datasets from any static host: no backend, no WASM, no HTTP Range requests. zonemapdb splits a dataset into many small whole files at build time, indexes them, and generates a typed TypeScript client that fetches only the files a query needs.
rules: Install with pnpm, two packages: `pnpm add zonemapdb && pnpm add -D zonemapdb-cli`. `zonemapdb` is the browser runtime (production dep); `zonemapdb-cli` is the Node build tool (devDep). Never use npm or yarn in examples.

The generated client is the only query API. Import it from the committed output: `import { connect } from './zonemapdb/client'` then `const db = connect()`. `connect()` with no arguments works for the standard deploy; override the location with `connect({ basePath: 'https://cdn.example.com/zonemapdb' })`.

Do NOT write SQL and do NOT invent a chained/builder query API. Queries are a single plain object with a Prisma-style `where`: `db.movies.findMany({ where: { year: { gte: 2000 } }, orderBy: { rating: 'desc' }, limit: 20 })`.

Query methods per collection are exactly: `findMany(args)` → `{ records, hasMore, total? }`; `count(where)` → `{ count, exact }` (an upper bound unless `exact`); `get(id)` → the record or `null` (only generated when the dataset has a primary key); `getSchema()` → the runtime schema descriptor. There is no `create`, `update`, `delete`, `upsert`, or `findUnique`.

Operators are per field type. string: `equals`, `not`, `in`, `contains`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`. number and date (ISO strings): `equals`, `not`, `in`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`. boolean: `equals`, `not`. A string sort field also gets `gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`. multi-valued (string[]): `some`, `every`, `hasEvery`, `isEmpty`, e.g. `{ genres: { some: 'Sci-Fi' } }`. Fields marked `nullable`/`absent` add `isNull`/`isAbsent`/`exists`. Every non-json field is queryable and usable in `orderBy`.

Every `findMany` `where` needs at least one filter that prunes (narrows which files are read): a filter on the sort field, or one an index answers on an indexed field. `not`, the missing-value operators, filters on unindexed fields, and `contains`/`endsWith` without their index opt-in are riders: allowed only beside a pruning filter. A rider-only `where` is a compile error and a `NEEDS_PRUNING` runtime error, unless you pass `scan: 'block-order'` with a `limit`. Check a runtime-built `where` with `wherePrunes(where, db.x.getSchema())`.
Boolean logic is implicit-AND across `where` keys only. There is NO `OR`, `AND`, or `NOT` key — express alternatives with multiple queries client-side.
Pagination is offset/limit only (`limit`, `offset`) — there are no cursors. `findMany` returns `hasMore` (computed via limit+1 over-fetch) for next-page detection.
zonemapdb is READ-ONLY from the browser. There is no way to mutate data at runtime; you update data by re-running `zonemapdb build` and redeploying.

CLI commands are `init`, `build`, and `inspect` (the `bin` is named `zonemapdb`; after installing, run `pnpm exec zonemapdb init`). `init` is the ONLY place schema inference happens; `build` replays the baked schema and fails loud on drift — it never re-infers. There is no standalone `generate` command.

`zonemapdb build` writes two outputs: the served data tree (default `public/zonemapdb/`, deploy it — do not commit) and the generated `schema.ts` + `client.ts` (default `src/zonemapdb/`, DO commit them). The served tree entry point is `manifest.json` (stable name); everything else is content-hashed and immutable.

Configuration lives in a single committed `zonemapdb.config.json` validated by the published `config.schema.json`. Precedence is CLI flags > config file > inferred defaults; every wizard choice has an equivalent flag, so `init --yes` plus flags runs with zero prompts.
The runtime is ESM-only, zero third-party dependencies, framework-agnostic (pure `fetch`), and runs in the browser, a Web Worker, or Node >= 20. There are no framework adapters.

Runtime errors are thrown as `ZonemapDbError` (with a `ZonemapDbErrorCode`). `connect()` asserts the runtime major version equals `manifest.formatVersion` and fails loud on a major mismatch — realign versions and re-run `zonemapdb build`.
